title: Variation and Survival
seo_title: Grade 3 Variation Worksheets: How Differences Help Animals and Plants Survive
standard_text: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how the variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on variation and survival (NGSS 3-LS4-2): camouflage, traits that give an advantage, attracting mates, and survival data tables. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Some differences help living things survive.
key_sub: Members of a species vary. A trait like camouflage or long roots can help some individuals survive and have young.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things of the same kind are not all exactly alike. These differences are called variation.

Some differences give an advantage: they help an individual survive, find a mate or have more young.

  • Camouflage: colors that blend in help animals hide from predators.
  • Longer spines, faster legs, thicker fur and longer roots help in some places.
  • Brighter feathers or louder calls can help animals attract mates.

Which trait is best depends on the environment: white fur helps in snow but not in a brown field.

Example

Green and brown beetles live on green leaves. Which survive better?

Green beetles blend in.

Birds see brown ones more easily.

Answer: the green beetles

Example

Why do some deer escape wolves better?

Some deer are faster.

Answer: Faster deer can run away.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all members of a species are exactly the same.
  • Thinking animals change their traits because they want to.
  • Forgetting that the best trait depends on the environment.

faq.a: Variation means the differences in traits among members of the same species, like fur color or speed.

faq.q: How can variation help an animal survive?
faq.a: A trait like camouflage, speed or thick fur can help it hide, escape or stay warm, so it is more likely to survive and have young.

faq.q: Does the best trait depend on the environment?
faq.a: Yes. White fur helps a rabbit hide in snow, but brown fur is better in a brown field.

items.q: Hana studies moths living on light, pale tree trunks. Some are light-colored and some are dark-colored. Which ones are more likely to survive?
items.e: The light moths blend in with the pale bark.

items.q: Why can small differences help an animal survive?
c: Some differences make it easier to find food, hide or stay warm.
items.e: Traits that help survival are an advantage.

items.q: Emma studies crabs living on a sandy beach. Some are red and some are sand-colored. Which ones are more likely to survive?
items.e: Sand-colored crabs blend in with the beach.

items.q: Sam sees that some frogs grow up with louder calls. Why might these frogs have more young?
c: It makes them hide from predators better.
Females find and choose males with louder calls.
All of them are exactly the same.
items.e: Females find and choose males with louder calls.

items.q: Eli studies frogs living on a muddy pond bank. Some are bright green and some are dull brown. Which ones are more likely to survive?
items.e: Brown frogs blend in with the mud.

items.q: Sofia studies rabbits living in snowy winter fields. Some are white and some are brown. Which ones are more likely to survive?
items.e: White rabbits blend in with the snow.

items.q: What is camouflage?
c: a color or pattern that helps a living thing blend in with its surroundings
items.e: Blending in helps animals hide from predators.

items.q: Does an animal change its color because it wants to blend in?
c: No. Animals are born with color differences, and some colors help more.
items.e: Variation is already there when the animals are born.

items.q: Which trait could help a male bird find a mate?
items.e: Bright colors and songs attract mates.
